title: Crude Oil Prices Came Back After the 20% Fee Plan Disappeared
part1:
The stage was the Strait of Hormuz. Here, political news and movements in crude oil prices appeared as if they had separate scripts.

The first to appear was President Trump, on July 13. He posted a proposal to charge all cargo passing through the strait a 20% fee to cover the cost of the United States ensuring the strait’s safety.

In other words, the plan was to have the cargo side cover the cost of protecting the strait. But it did not explain who would collect the fee, who would pay it, or how the amount would be calculated. No details of the system were given.
part2:
The next day, the scene suddenly changed. President Trump posted that he was withdrawing the 20% plan and replacing it with Gulf states’ trade and investment deals with the United States. He also told reporters that ships passing through the strait should not be charged a fee, and that he did not like the idea of a fee itself.

This is where the crude oil market took a slightly surprising turn. After the announcement, Brent crude futures briefly gave up some of their gains. However, before long, they returned to a high level close to where they had been before the announcement.

When this was reported, Brent crude futures were about 2.6% higher than the day before and had risen above $85 a barrel. The settlement price after trading ended was also $84.73 a barrel, up 1.7% from the day before.
part3:
If we follow only the headlines, it may seem that crude oil prices would also settle down because the 20% fee plan was gone. In fact, however, the gains narrowed after the announcement, and then returned to a high level.

During that time, some information was still waiting in the wings: attacks by the United States and Iran, a naval blockade, and concerns about tanker safety. Even after the fee plan was replaced by investment deals, such news continued.

So we cannot determine the relationship between the withdrawal and prices from this movement alone. What we can confirm is that even after the political script was rewritten, worries at sea remained on the same stage.

The crude oil market is not a drama that moves forward based only on the words in a post. Beyond the screen, there was also the question of whether tankers could pass safely. That information, too, was part of the same scene.
in_one_line: Crude oil prices returned to high levels even after Trump withdrew the 20% fee plan, while worries at sea remained.
